nodes.description: Selective pan-FGFR1-4 small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor approved for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with susceptible FGFR3 or FGFR2 genetic alterations following prior systemic therapy, achieving a 40% confirmed response rate in BLC2001 and significantly prolonging overall survival over chemotherapy in phase 3 THOR Cohort 1 (median 12.1 vs 7.8 months). On-target hyperphosphatemia from renal FGFR1 inhibition is the most common treatment-related adverse event (77% in BLC2001) and guides pharmacodynamic dose titration alongside stomatitis, diarrhea, and central serous retinopathy monitoring.

evidence.reference_title: Erdafitinib in Locally Advanced or Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma.
evidence.snippet: The use of erdafitinib was associated with an objective tumor response in 40% of previously treated patients who had locally advanced and unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with FGFR alterations.

evidence.reference_title: Phase 3 THOR Japanese subgroup analysis: erdafitinib in advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer and fibroblast growth factor receptor alterations
evidence.snippet: In the THOR trial (NCT03390504) Cohort 1, erdafitinib demonstrated significantly prolonged overall survival (OS) (median 12.1 versus 7.8 months) and reduced risk of death by 36% (hazard ratio 0.64, P = 0.005) compared with chemotherapy in metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) patients with FGFR alterations who progressed after ≥ 1 prior treatments, including anti-PD-(L)1.

evidence.snippet: The most common adverse events of any grade include: hyperphosphatemia (77%), stomatitis (58%), diarrhea (51%), dry mouth (46%), decreased appetite (38%), dysgeusia (37%), fatigue (32%), dry skin (32%) and alopecia (29%). Ocular toxicities of any grade occurred in 51% of patients including: central serous retinopathy (21%), dry eye (19%), blurred vision (17%), cataracts (6%), and keratitis (5%).

nodes.description: PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade (including pembrolizumab, alone or combined with enfortumab vedotin) is standard systemic immunotherapy in advanced urothelial carcinoma and is sequenced prior to erdafitinib in FGFR-altered metastatic disease; in phase 3 THOR Cohort 2, PD-(L)1-naive patients with FGFR-altered metastatic urothelial cancer had comparable overall survival with erdafitinib and pembrolizumab (10.9 vs 11.1 months).

evidence.reference_title: Advances in diagnosis and treatment of bladder cancer.
evidence.snippet: In this cohort, 351 pretreated, PDL1 naive patients with advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer with select FGFR alterations were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive erdafitinib daily versus pembrolizumab. With a median follow-up of 33 months, median overall survival with erdafitinib and pembrolizumab was 10.9 and 11.1 months, respectively, with a hazard ratio of 1.18 (95% confidence interval 0.92 to 1.51, p=0.18).
